findings.what: The theme keeps one note ringing: each new note damps the one before (30 ms raised cosine, the engine's steal fade) as a harpist damps a staccato line; the coda's chords keep four. listen.cap is now one value per crossing (theme 1, coda 4) from the score's strings {theme: 1, coda: 4}; harpStep reads cap[k].
findings.evidence: Recording: loudest ringing 2nd at onset + 50 ms is -25.1 dB at worst, 0 of 60 seconds-cases over -20 dB (want <= -20). Engine stat: at most 4 strings at once.

findings.what: One string a note: the octave for small speakers is the string's own 2nd partial at dbl (0.56, -5 dB) of the fundamental, with the fundamental's decay, so it is a steady doubling; no second string, no near-unison. Tuned harp strings have harmonic partials (exactly n f) and fixed start phases (by the partial's odd part, so n and 2n start alike), not random ones.
findings.evidence: Octave level over each theme note: -6.29 to -4.04 dB (spread 2.25, want within +-1.5). Final chord ring-out: B4 3.0, D5 0.1, F#5 2.3 dB after the decay trend, monotone in B4 and D5 (want <= 3; round 2: 29-31 dB). t_seasong checks one string a note, dbl exact, harmonic partials, fixed phases.

findings.what: The pointer harp's D accent is folded into its D4 copy: one string at hypot(w, 0.5) of the note's level (the power two independent strings have on average), never a second string at the same pitch. Each octave copy starts a quarter turn on from the copy below, so its partials meet the lower copy's in quadrature and add in power every time; no random phase decides a crossing's balance.
findings.evidence: Seeds 1-8 in the lab: D - E 2.58 to 3.67 dB, E within 1.2 dB (round 2: D - E -0.5 to +6.6, E 4.3 dB). The D4 copy is one deterministic string, so repeated identical D crossings differ only by the strings' own +-1 dB; with |F| = 1 its level is 1.26 hypot(0.36, 0.5) = 0.78 of the note's against E's E4 copy 0.49: +4.0 dB (want >= +2). Re-recorded by the verifier on the pointer loop (review-verify/pointer.m4a): D4 within 0.7 dB loop to loop, 5.2 to 5.7 dB over the E4 copy. t_seasong: a D has one string a pitch.

findings.what: No random detune for a piece's notes: a pitch is always the same frequency (MIDI with the score's tuning). Each string carries its note as a key, and the worklet damps a string plucked again before it sounds (30 ms), as a harpist re-plucks one string. In the theme the cap of 1 also damps every re-strike.
findings.evidence: t_seasong: every string keyed by its note; exact pitches (0 cents off the tuned value). Recording ring-out shows no swell (B4, D5 no rise).

findings.what: The score's tuning: F# is a just fifth over B (+1.955 cents), every other pitch equal temperament. With harmonic partials, B3's 3rd partial is exactly F#4's 2nd: the final chord's fifth does not beat. 2 cents is inaudible in the melody.

findings.what: The generator now reports the drawing in screen terms (look: the most it turns within 4 px of arc at 128 px a unit, its smallest radius, the narrowest gap between turns) instead of only turnMaxDeg. The curve itself is unchanged.
findings.evidence: Report: 33.3 deg within 4 px at 128 px/unit, smallest radius 6.1 px (the review's 33 deg / 4.4-6 px). Why not fixed: the bends are where the phase must cover a 4-semitone leap plus a turn within one eighth of statement 3 (F# D F#, C# E#, E C) at the curve's constant speed. A search over the phase design (turn travel 0.06 to 0.16, room 0.42 to 0.8, eased turns, crossing slope 0.5 to 0.8) gave at best 28 deg; more travel or a lower slope made it worse or infeasible (no constant-speed solution). z^(-3+48i) is not usable: the GPU's float32 z^alpha needs |beta theta| < 88 on the branch, and beta = 48 gives up to 48 pi = 151. Fixing it needs a new phase design (a minimum-acceleration phase through the notes), a round of its own.

findings.status: rejected with evidence, for the user
findings.what: Measured now (look.gapPx, 4.2 px at 128 px/unit between the curve's end and the third turn); the coda not changed.
findings.evidence: An ascending octave roll multiplies r by e^(2 pi/24) = 1.30, which is exactly the spacing between turns, so the last up-roll always comes back to the turn outside it unless theta advances by most of a turn while it rolls. Search: a shorter tail gives 5.5 px; 10 px needs a much slower coda (codaSlow 2.0, rolls 0.45 beat: 8.6 px, +1 s). The options that work change the music the user approved: end on a falling roll (B4 F#4 D4 B3) or on a three-note chord. Left for the user to choose.
